rationale: Wikipedia gives the reflexive/symmetric/transitive definition and [a] = {x : a ~ x} in exactly this form. The item merges relation, class, representative, quotient set and quotient map into one definition and adds the library notation A/~ and pi; content and conventions unchanged, so ai-altered rather than literature-derived.

Sourced: "every element x of X belongs to one and only one equivalence class", "x ~ y iff [x] = [y]", and the converse that every partition induces an equivalence relation whose blocks are its classes. The item merges these into one lemma and adds an explicit UNIQUENESS clause (only one equivalence relation has a given quotient set), which is the standard bijection between partitions and equivalence relations spelled out. Proof is locally written.

Sourced: binary operation as a map S x S -> S (closure built in), and the associativity/commutativity equations. The item merges these with the closed-subset/induced-operation paragraph that Wikipedia states by example; no changed quantifiers or hypotheses.

The three definitions match the source clause for clause: left identity "e * s = s for all s in S", right identity "s * e = s for all s in S", two-sided identity "both a left identity and a right identity". Same quantifiers, same conventions, cosmetic wording only.

Sourced statement: "if l is a left identity and r is a right identity, then l = l * r = r" and "there can never be more than one two-sided identity". The item states that sharp form and adds consequence 2 (a two-sided identity is the unique one-sided identity on either side), an immediate merge, so ai-altered. The proof is the sourced two-readings argument on e * f, adapted to the library step format, hence ai-altered rather than ai-generated.

Sourced: monoid as associativity plus a two-sided identity, and submonoid as a subset containing e and closed under the operation. The item merges semigroup, monoid, commutative/abelian and submonoid into one definition and carries the identity in the triple (M,*,e); no content change.

Sourced: left/right/two-sided inverse and "an element u of a ring R is a unit if there exists v with vu = uv = 1". The item states these for a monoid and fixes the notation M^x for the set of units; same conventions (h is a left inverse of g when h*g = e).

Sourced: "In the common case where the operation is associative, the left and right inverse of an element are equal and unique", with the displayed proof l = l * (x * r) = (l * x) * r = r; and "every element has at most one inverse" for monoids. The item adds numbered consequences 1-3 (a one-sided equation identifies the inverse; left plus right inverse implies invertible), which is the same content unfolded. The proof follows the sourced argument, so ai-altered.

Sourced: the group axioms (associativity, identity, inverses) and the definition of abelian. The item presents a group as a monoid all of whose elements are invertible and then writes out (G1)-(G3); an equivalent standard presentation, merged with the notation paragraph.

Sourced: e^-1 = e, (g^-1)^-1 = g and the socks-and-shoes law (gh)^-1 = h^-1 g^-1 are standard consequences stated on the group article. Claim 4, that (gh)^-1 = g^-1 h^-1 holds exactly when g and h commute, is the standard characterisation of when the reversal may be dropped; it is stated here as a biconditional and both directions are proved locally (steps 3.1, 3.2). Proof written locally.

Sourced: "if a * b = a * c then b = c" in a group, and that left/right multiplication by a group element is a bijection. The item merges cancellation, the translation bijections with their explicit inverse maps, and unique solubility of gx = h and xg = h into one lemma. Proof written locally.

Sourced: "The set of all invertible elements in a monoid, together with the operation, forms a group" and "The set of units of R forms a group under multiplication". The item adds the equivalence "M is a group exactly when M^x = M", an immediate merge. Proof written locally, including the step that the witness inverse lies inside M^x.

Sourced: "the group whose elements are all bijective functions from X to X and whose group operation is that of function composition". Convention deltas recorded: the item defines Sym(X) for an ARBITRARY set X, not only a finite one, fixes (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)) (right factor acts first), and adds cycle/transposition notation for a finite list of distinct points.

Sourced: Sym(X) is a group under composition, and S_n is abelian if and only if n <= 2. Convention delta: the item states non-abelianness with THREE NAMED PAIRWISE DISTINCT POINTS of an arbitrary X rather than a cardinality hypothesis, which is strictly weaker to assume and avoids any counting; the witness pair (a b), (b c) is the standard one. Proof written locally.

Sourced: the finite product in a monoid and "the empty product is by convention equal to the multiplicative identity". Delta: here the empty product is not a convention but the base clause of a recursion, and well-definedness is discharged through the library recursion theorem on N x M with von Neumann naturals; the underlying object is the standard iterated product.

Sourced: the generalized associative law ("repeated application of the operation produces the same result regardless of how valid pairs of parentheses are inserted") and Bourbaki, Algebra I, Ch. I sec. 1.3, which proves the associativity theorem for a finite sequence cut into consecutive blocks and the commutativity theorem for permuted factors. Convention delta recorded: the library introduces no formal syntax of bracketed expressions, so "bracketing does not matter" is rendered as the explicit block/regrouping law with cut points s_j and block lengths c_j, plus the splitting law; claim 3 is Bourbaki commutativity. Proof written locally.

Sourced: g^0 = identity, natural powers by recursion, and negative powers as inverses of positive ones. Delta: the item splits on the SIGN of the integer using the library embedding iota : N -> Z rather than on a representative of the equivalence class, and proves the two readings of g^{iota(k)} agree; standard object, library-specific well-definedness.

Sourced: b^m b^n = b^{m+n}, (b^m)^n = b^{mn}, and b^n c^n = (bc)^n with the explicit caveat "this formula is true only if the summands commute". The item states the four unconditional laws plus the commuting-hypothesis law, over integer exponents in a group and natural exponents in a monoid. Proof written locally around the normal form g^x = g^a (g^b)^{-1}.

Sourced: the subgroup notion. Convention delta recorded: Wikipedia defines a subgroup as "a subset whose members form a group with respect to the group operation in G", whereas the item defines it by the three closure conditions (S1)-(S3); the two are reconciled inside the library by lem-subgroup-criterion, so this is a presentation choice, not a content change.

Sourced: the one-step test, "For every a and b in H, the element ab^-1 is in H", for a nonempty subset H. The item merges it with a second claim, that a nonempty subset which is a group under the restricted operation carries the identity and the inverses of G; that reconciliation is what makes its (S1)-(S3) definition agree with the source definition of subgroup. Proof written locally.

Sourced: "The intersection of subgroups A and B of G is again a subgroup of G". Delta, and a strengthening in the safe direction: the item states it for an arbitrary NONEMPTY family and flags the nonemptiness hypothesis as load bearing (the empty intersection is not a subset of G under the conventions used here). Proof written locally.

Sourced: <S> as "the smallest subgroup of G containing every element of S", equivalently "the intersection over all subgroups containing the elements of S", and the definitions of cyclic subgroup and cyclic group. The item takes the intersection form as primary and derives the smallest-subgroup property; it also derives <empty> = {e} rather than stipulating it.
Sourced: "<g> = { g^k | k in Z }" and "Every cyclic group is abelian". The item merges the two into one lemma and proves both inclusions separately. Proof written locally.

Sourced: "Given two integers a and b, with b != 0, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, and 0 <= r < |b|". Convention delta recorded: the item SPECIALISES to b > 0 with 0 <= r < b, because no absolute value on Z exists at this point in the library reading order, and it also defines b | a for use on the page. A specialisation with unchanged content, hence ai-altered. Proof written locally from the ordered-ring axioms and well-ordering.

Sourced: in a finite group every element has finite order, i.e. some positive power is the identity. Delta: the item proves it by applying the sharpest pigeonhole claim directly to k |-> beta(g^k) from sigma(m) to m, deliberately avoiding "a subset of a finite set is finite", which is not yet available; the statement itself is the standard one. Proof written locally.

Sourced: |G| as the number of elements of a finite group, and ord(a) as "the smallest positive integer m such that a^m = e", infinite otherwise. Convention deltas recorded: |G| is the unique von Neumann natural equinumerous with G (uniqueness discharged by the pigeonhole lemma), min S_g is supplied by the well-ordering principle, and the symbol infinity is reserved and carries no arithmetic.

Sourced: "a^k = e if and only if ord(a) divides k" and "ord(a) = ord(<a>)". The item merges these with distinctness of g^0,...,g^{n-1} and the infinite-order dichotomy into one lemma, and states the divisibility clause over integer exponents. Proof written locally, driven by division with remainder.

Sourced: a group homomorphism is "a function h : G -> H such that for all u and v in G it holds that h(u*v) = h(u).h(v)", and a monoid homomorphism additionally satisfies f(e_M) = e_N, "the latter condition cannot be omitted". The item states both and merges in the endomorphism/composition remarks; no content change.

Sourced: "h maps the identity element e_G of G to the identity element e_H of H" and "h(u^-1) = h(u)^-1"; and, for the monoid clause, "the latter condition cannot be omitted". Delta: claim 3, f(g^n) = f(g)^n for every integer n, was not located on the cited pages; it is the standard immediate induction from (H1) together with claims 1 and 2 and is proved here in steps 3.2, 4.1 and 5.1, so the item as a whole remains a recoverable restatement of established material. Proof written locally.

Sourced: a field "is a group under addition, with additive identity called 0" and "the nonzero elements form a group under multiplication", together with the no-zero-divisors argument b = (a^-1 a)b = a^-1(ab) = 0. The item specialises this to Q and R via the library field theorems. Verification written locally.

Sourced: "In the ring of integers Z, the only units are 1 and -1", and Z as a commutative ring whose additive structure is an abelian group. The item merges the three claims and proves the unit computation from the order rather than quoting it. Verification written locally.

Sourced: "The set of nonnegative integers under addition is a cancellative monoid", the standard witness that cancellativity is strictly weaker than invertibility. The item states the refuted claim explicitly and supplies (N,+,0) with 1 as the non-invertible witness. Refutation written locally.

Sourced: congruence modulo n as an equivalence relation, Z/nZ as the set of congruence classes with well-defined addition, and "Under addition, Z/mZ is a cyclic group" of order n generated by the class of 1. Delta: the item carries n >= 1 explicitly in the title and statement and disposes of n = 0 separately, and uses only division with remainder (no gcd). Verification written locally.

Sourced: S3 has six elements, is the first nonabelian symmetric group, and its elements are the identity (order 1), three transpositions (order 2) and two 3-cycles (order 3). Delta: the item works with the specific set {1,2,3} of von Neumann naturals and proves exhaustiveness of the six listed triples by hand. Verification written locally.

Sourced: the exponent law (bc)^n = b^n c^n is "true only if the summands commute", and S3 is non-abelian with the transpositions as witnesses. The witness pair g = (1 2), h = (2 3) with n = 2 is a directly checkable instance of that caveat rather than a new claim. Refutation written locally.

The source states exactly this realisation: "The identity and double-transpositions of four objects form V", i.e. {(), (1,2)(3,4), (1,3)(2,4), (1,4)(2,3)} inside S4; four elements; abelian, with "composing any two of the three non-identity elements produces the third one" (the item multiplication table); "All non-identity elements of the Klein group have order 2"; and "The Klein four-group is the smallest non-cyclic group". Same hypotheses, same conventions, cosmetic differences only. Verification written locally.

Sourced: the dihedral group of order 8, presentation r^4 = s^2 = 1 with srs = r^-1 (equivalently sr = r^-1 s), elements {e, r, r^2, r^3, s, rs, r^2 s, r^3 s}, non-abelian, the symmetry group of the square; and the standard graph-theoretic fact Aut(C_n) = D_n, which is claim 4 at n = 4. Convention delta recorded: the square is COMBINATORIAL here (a 4-cycle edge relation on {1,2,3,4}), not Euclidean, because R^2 is not available at this point in the reading order, so claim 4 is Aut(C_4) = D_4 rendered as a permutation identity. Verification written locally.

Sourced: "all subgroups of Z are of the form <m> = mZ" and every subgroup of a cyclic group is cyclic. Delta: the item states the converse half with n >= 0, identifies n as the least positive element of H when H is nontrivial, and handles H = {0} separately. Verification written locally, driven by the least-positive-element argument and division with remainder.

Sourced: the nonnegative integers under addition are a submonoid of (Z,+) that is not a group ("the non-negative integers form a cancellative monoid under addition ... yet lack additive inverses required for group structure"), which is exactly the witness used. The refuted claim (nonempty + contains the identity + closed under the operation implies subgroup) is the standard motivation for testing xy^-1 rather than xy. Refutation written locally. Note: the Cancellation_property URL is the sharpest support and is NOT currently in this item sources.references; the two URLs that are there also return 200.

The source states the false claim, the exact criterion and the exact witness: "The union of subgroups A and B is a subgroup if and only if A subset B or B subset A", with the counterexample that 2Z union 3Z is not a subgroup of Z because 2 and 3 lie in it but 5 does not. The item reproduces that statement, that witness and that criterion with no change of hypotheses or conventions. Refutation written locally.
